{{Short description|Greek computer scientist}}
{{For|the football player|Ilias Koutsoupias}}
'''Elias Koutsoupias''' is a [[Greece|Greek]] computer scientist working in [[algorithmic game theory]]. 

== Education ==
Koutsoupias received his bachelor's degree in electrical engineering from the [[National Technical University of Athens]] and his doctorate in computer science in 1994 from the [[University of California, San Diego]] under the supervision of [[Christos Papadimitriou]].<ref>{{MathGenealogyProject|id=70502}}</ref><ref name="personalwebsite">{{citation|url=http://www.cs.ox.ac.uk/people/elias.koutsoupias/Personal/|title=Personal website|access-date=2019-07-07}}</ref> He subsequently taught at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]], the [[University of Athens]], and is now a professor at the [[University of Oxford]].<ref name="personalwebsite"/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://simons.berkeley.edu/people/elias-koutsoupias|title=Elias Koutsoupias|publisher=Simons Institute for the Theory of Computing}}</ref>

== Career ==
In 2012, he was one of the recipients of the [[Gödel Prize]] for his contributions to [[algorithmic game theory]], specifically the introduction of the [[price of anarchy]] concept with Papadimitriou in the paper 'Worst-case equilibria'.{{sfnp|Koutsoupias|Papadimitriou|1999}}<ref> {{cite web|title=Gödel Prize, ACM |url=http://eatcs.org/index.php/goedel-prize | publisher=European Association for Theoretical Computer Science }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.icsi.berkeley.edu/icsi/news/2012/07/papadimitriou-receives-goedel-prize|title=Faculty Associate Receives 2012 Goedel Prize|publisher=University of California, Berkeley}}</ref> His work has also spanned [[Computational complexity theory|complexity theory]], [[design and analysis of algorithms]], [[online algorithms]], [[computer networks|networks]], uncertainty decisions and [[mathematical economics]].<ref name="personalwebsite"/> In 2019, he gave a lecture on [[game theory]] at [[CERN]].<ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Fshzxy9LdFI |title= Elias Koutsoupias: Game Theory 1/2 🎲 CERN |last= Koutsoupias |first= Elias |date= 6 February 2019|website= www.youtube.com/watch?v=Fshzxy9LdFI |publisher= CERN Lectures |access-date= 22 August 2019 }}</ref>

In 2016, Koutsoupias worked with [[Aggelos Kiayias]], Maria Kyropoulou and Yiannis Tselekounis, on the paper “Blockchain Mining Games”. He contributed aspects of game theory for stake pools in the [[Ouroboros (protocol)|Ouroboros]] consensus protocol. This was used in the [[Cardano (blockchain platform)|Cardano]] blockchain, and Koutsoupias became a senior research fellow at IOHK, the blockchain engineering company developing Cardano.<ref>Aggelos Kiayias, Elias Koutsoupias, Maria Kyropoulou and Yiannis Tselekounis (2016) “Blockchain Mining Games”, in EC '16: Proceedings of the 2016 ACM Conference on Economics and Computation, July 2016, pages 365–382. https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/2940716.2940773</ref><ref>Lars Brünjes; Aggelos Kiayias; Elias Koutsoupias; Aikaterini-Panagiota Stouka (2020) “Reward Sharing Schemes for Stake Pools”, 2020 IEEE European Symposium on Security and Privacy (EuroS&P). https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/abstract/document/9230398</ref><ref>IOHK team page, https://iohk.io/en/team/elias-koutsoupias</ref>
